title: Response Tiles and Client Synthesis PRD (draft)
body:
Purpose
This PRD proposes a new lightweight streaming primitive for the Hosted API called "response tiles" and an SDK synthesis model that lets clients compose, speculatively execute, and deterministically reconcile partial results and tool calls. The goal is to improve latency & robustness for low-bandwidth/edge clients, enable incremental structured output validation, and provide clear semantics for partial tool invocations without adding a heavyweight session layer.

Problem statement
Current incremental streaming approaches return a flat text stream or partially-structured chunks with weak commit semantics. This makes it hard for mobile/edge SDKs to:
- Show deterministic UI updates while offline or under flaky networks.
- Speculatively call local tool proxies (e.g., search, browser, connectors) and reconcile results when final tiles arrive.
- Verify structured responses incrementally with a schema without risking double-execution of side-effecting tool calls.

High-level idea
Introduce small, resolved units called "tiles": self-describing fragments of the final response (content + metadata). Tiles have deterministic ids, explicit lifecycle (tentative -> committed/aborted), and optional tool invocation frames. SDKs receive tiles over the streaming channel, can render them immediately, and may trigger local speculative tool calls guarded by a tile-level idempotency token. When a committed tile arrives, the SDK reconciles speculative outputs with the server's authoritative tile and either keeps local results (if safe) or rolls back using idempotent semantics.

Goals and success metrics
- End-to-end median UI latency reduction for first useful content by 20% for mobile clients.
- Mobile edge reconnection success: 95% of sessions can resume and render committed tiles without duplication.
- Tool safety: no more than 0.1% of speculative tool calls result in unsafe side-effects measured in integration tests.
- Observability: introduce tile_commit_latency and tile_reconciliation_rate metrics in Console.

Non-goals
- Not replacing session-resume or full blob checkpointing for long-running multimodal jobs.
- Not designing a monolithic workflow engine. Tiles are scoped to single request responses.

User stories
1) As a product engineer building a chat on mobile, I want the client to show parts of the answer immediately while guaranteeing no duplicate database writes from speculative tool calls.
2) As an SRE, I want telemetry to indicate how often speculative reconciliation diverges so we can tune SLOs.
3) As an SDK author, I want a small ergonomic API that exposes tile events and idempotency tokens without forcing users to understand the server internals.

API surface (sketch)
- Streaming payload: each message is a tile envelope with fields: tile_id, status (tentative|committed|aborted), schema_hint, content_fragment, tooling_frame(optional), idempotency_token(optional), checksum.
- REST fallback: final response contains an ordered list of committed tiles for clients that do not support streaming.
- Tooling frame: describes expected side-effects (type: read|nonmutating_call|mutating_call, canonical_tool_id, call_args_schema).

SDK ergonomics
- Minimal callback API: onTile(tileEnvelope) -> returns SDK mayRespond(speculativeHandler) helper.
- Speculative helper returns an idempotency token bound to tile_id, with helpers to mark speculative results as tentative or finalized.
- Higher-level bindings: JS/Android/iOS SDKs provide a small "tile renderer" component that maps schema_hint -> validator and a "tool proxy" shim for local connectors.
- Backpressure: SDKs can acknowledge a max in-flight tentative tile budget; server adjusts batching.

Deterministic reconciliation rules
- If a speculative tool call uses the server-provided idempotency token and a tool is mutating, the server will respond with a reconciliation outcome in the committed tile (match|replace|abort).
- When reconcile=replace, SDK should surface a rollback hook; the SDK runtime must provide a transactional wrapper for common local connectors (cache + compensating action stubs).

Security & safety
- Speculative mutating calls are disabled by default in hosted mode. Projects may opt-in and must enable enterprise policy flags.
- Tooling frames must declare call type and be validated by server-side safety checks prior to providing idempotency tokens.

Observability & debugging
- New telemetry: tile_latency, speculative_call_count, reconcile_divergence_rate, tile_loss_rate.
- Console: per-request tile timeline (tentative -> committed) with side-by-side speculative call logs and reconciliation outcomes.

Compatibility and rollout strategy
Phase 0 (experimental, internal): implement server tile framing and CLI + integration tests. SDKs: JS internal alpha (dev channel).
Phase 1 (beta): enable public JS/Android SDKs with default speculative disabled and opt-in config. Expose telemetry.
Phase 2 (GA): enable opt-in mutating speculation for Dedicated/Private with enterprise review; rollout to Hosted with guardrails.

Testing plan
- Unit tests: tile lifecycle transitions, checksum and idempotency behavior.
- Integration: simulate flaky streams + reconnection and verify no duplicates for sample connector.
- Chaos: loss or reordering of tentative tiles and validation against reconciliation logic.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- How large should tiles be? Too small increases overhead; too large reduces responsiveness. Proposal: default tile target ~400-800 tokens with server-side heuristics.
- Should speculative read-only calls be automatically merged on commit? We propose conservative default: keep speculative results only if server reconciliation signals exact-match or superset.
- Billing semantics for speculative tool calls need legal/product review.

Milestones (90d)
- Week 2: server framing prototype + e2e test harness.
- Week 5: JS SDK alpha (internal) and CLI validation.
- Week 8: Beta SDKs + Console telemetry prototype.
- Week 12: Public beta with opt-in flag.

Appendix: example flow
1) Client initiates streaming call. Server streams tile A (tentative, summary), client renders and optionally calls a local search shim with token A_tkn.
2) Server streams tile B (tentative, embedded tool frame says nonmutating:browser_lookup). Client uses local browser connector; speculative result cached.
3) Server commits tile A with checksum match -> client marks speculative results as authoritative.
4) Server commits tile B with replace -> client invalidates speculative result and shows server content.

Next steps
- Align with Console & telemetry owners on tile-grade metrics.
- Engineering spike to measure overhead of tile framing on 99th percentile latency.
- Legal/product review of billing and mutating speculation.

Notes
This draft intentionally emphasizes a tiny, composable primitive (tiles) instead of a heavy session API. It aims to be pragmatic for mobile-first SDKs while giving product teams explicit reconciliation semantics for tool-calling integrations.
